title: Trump Attacks Commerce Department Over GDP Revisions, Demands Probe into 'Fake' Economic Data
snippet: President Donald Trump has accused the Commerce Department of purposefully suppressing strong GDP data before the midterms, demanding an immediate investigation into federal economic figures.
content:
WEST PALM BEACH, Fla. — President Donald Trump renewed his attacks on federal statistical agencies on Thursday, claiming without evidence that the Commerce Department intentionally suppressed strong economic growth figures ahead of the recent midterm elections to undermine Republicans.

Writing on social media over the Thanksgiving holiday, Trump alleged that pre-election gross domestic product reports were "FAKE" and demanded an "immediate investigation" into why updated, stronger figures were not released prior to Election Day.

Controversy Over Routine Revisions

The president's outburst stems from a report issued Wednesday by the Commerce Department's Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA). The agency updated its third-quarter GDP growth estimate to an annualized rate of 4.3%, up from a preliminary estimate of 3.4%. Federal statistical agencies routinely update economic calculations as more complete data becomes available, operating on strict, pre-announced schedules independent of the political calendar.

Despite this standard protocol, Trump labeled the initial estimate a "massive, and purposeful, error" meant to influence the Nov. 3 midterms, in which Democrats won control of Congress. Neither the Commerce Department nor the BEA immediately responded to requests for comment on the holiday.

Pattern of Challenging Official Metrics

Thursday's statement marks the latest instance of the president questioning official government data that clashes with his political narrative. In August 2025, Trump ousted the commissioner of the Bureau of Labor Statistics after a disappointing employment report showed weaker job growth than expected, calling those figures "phony" and "rigged."

Economists and market analysts have repeatedly warned that undermining the credibility of nonpartisan statistical agencies risks unsettling financial markets and damaging business confidence, as investors rely heavily on neutral baseline data from agencies like the BEA and BLS.

Voters Signal Persistent Economic Stress

While Trump insists his administration has driven an unprecedented economic surge, polling suggests voters view the economic climate far less favorably. According to AP Voter Poll data from the midterms, roughly 76% of voters described economic conditions as "not so good" or "poor," with a majority attributing ongoing inflation to White House policies.

Notably, Trump's social media post ignored other figures released alongside the GDP revision on Wednesday. Those reports showed the personal consumption expenditures price index—the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation metric—accelerated to an annual pace of 3.8% in October, highlighting persistent cost-of-living pressures facing American families.
